Walmart announces it will officially begin supporting Apple Pay next week. The retailer has refused to offer Apple Pay support for years, despite significant consumer pressure.

Apple Pay 終於登陸沃爾瑪

Walmart announced the news via a press release today. Starting August 24, the company will introduce contactless payment options — including Apple Pay — at select Walmart and Sam's Club locations. The feature will roll out to all U.S. stores by the end of this year and expand to gas stations by mid-2027.

Walmart is adding full contactless payment support covering Apple Pay on iPhone and Apple Watch, Google Pay, tap-to-pay credit and debit cards, and other payment platforms. Customers will also be able to add their Walmart and Sam's Club membership cards to platforms like Apple Wallet. Contactless payment will operate alongside existing payment methods, including Walmart's own payment service, Walmart Pay.

該公司表示：

Walmart is one of the last major retailers that has not supported Apple Pay, making this significant news for consumers. For years, the retailer has refused to offer contactless payments, sticking with its QR code-based Walmart Pay system.

Last year, Walmart was still doubling down, arguing that Walmart Pay was more convenient for customers than Apple Pay. However, to use Walmart Pay, customers had to first link a debit or credit card within the Walmart app on iPhone, then scan a QR code at checkout to complete the payment using their iPhone.

A quick search on social media reveals just how frustrated users have been with Walmart's refusal to support Apple Pay.

After all, most other longtime Apple Pay holdouts — including Kroger, Home Depot, and H-E-B — caved and added support years ago.

Does Walmart's lack of Apple Pay support affect your shopping habits? Now that they're rolling it out, are you more likely to shop at Walmart and Sam's Club? Let us know in the comments.
